How the NHL playoff simulator works

Every game on the 2026-27 schedule is played out 10,000 times. A game that is already final keeps its real result, including whether it went past regulation. Every other game is decided by the same calibrated win probability the NHL Simulator reports for that matchup, and by how often that matchup reaches overtime, because the team that loses in overtime or a shootout still takes a point.

The 2026-27 season is 84 games per team, 1,344 games in all, and every one of them is on the schedule the simulator reads.

The 2026-27 NHL playoff format

Teams earn two points for a win and one for a loss in overtime or a shootout. The top three teams in each of the 4 divisions make the playoffs, and the next two teams in each conference by points take the wild cards. The division winner with more points plays the second wild card, the other division winner plays the first, and the second and third place teams in each division meet. The bracket stays inside the division through the second round, and every series is best of seven with home ice to the team with more points.

How accurate is it

Hockey is the hardest of the four to forecast, and this page says so with numbers rather than adjectives. The engine's calibrated probability scored a Brier of 0.24727 on an untouched 2025-26 season, against 0.25000 for a coin flip. Two replacements were measured on that same season on 2026-09-15, a recalibrated Elo with rest and back to backs (0.24940) and the frozen V2 anchor (0.24856), and both were worse, so nothing was changed. The engine keeps the job until something beats it.

Tiebreakers

Ties in points are settled by regulation wins, then by points in the games between the tied teams, then by a random draw. The NHL's later steps, such as goal differential, are not applied, and they are listed here rather than approximated.

What the projection does not know

The model rates teams on results already played. A trade, a signing or an injury changes a team's rating only once games are played with it, so early in the season a team that rebuilt over the summer is rated on the roster it had. The win probability for a game in March does not know rest, back to backs or the starting goalie that night. The model data was last built Wednesday, September 16, 2026 at 8:01 AM PT.

NHL Playoff Simulator FAQ

How does the NHL playoff simulator work?

It plays out the rest of the 2026-27 regular season, seeds each conference with the real NHL format, and then plays every series game by game, best of seven, with home ice to the better regular season team. It repeats that 10,000 times and counts how often each team reaches each round.

How are the NHL wild cards decided?

After the top three teams in each division, the next two teams in each conference by points are the wild cards. The division winner with more points plays the second wild card.

Who is favored to win the Stanley Cup?

In the current projection the Colorado Avalanche win it 20% of the time, ahead of the Carolina Hurricanes at 8%. Those numbers move as results come in.

Why does the simulated bracket change each time?

A single bracket is one season out of thousands. The odds table is the summary of all of them; the bracket shows what one of those seasons looked like.

Is it free?

The published odds and bracket are free to read with no account. Running your own set needs a free account and uses the daily free simulator run.
